title: Variables
description: How to store a value and give it a name so you can use it later.

content.text: The label on the box is the variable's name. What's inside is its value. Whenever you use the name, Python opens the box and hands you the value.

parts.label: name
parts.note: The label you choose. You'll use it to get the value back later.

parts.label: store
parts.note: The assignment sign. It puts the value on the right into the box named on the left.

parts.label: value
parts.note: What goes in the box. It can be a number, some text, and more.

content.title: What Python is holding now
content.caption: Three variables, three boxes. `print(score)` opens the `score` box and shows `100`.

content.question: After `apples = 5`, what does `print(apples)` show?
content.explain: `print` opens the box named `apples` and shows what is inside it: `5`.

items.title: Good names
items.text: Letters, digits and underscores. Start with a letter.

items.title: Not allowed
items.text: No starting with a digit, no spaces, no dashes.

content.question: Which one is a valid variable name?
content.explain: `player_score` uses only letters and an underscore. The others start with a digit, have a space, or use a dash.

items: A variable can get a new value at any time.
The new value **replaces** the old one. The old one is gone.
The name stays the same: only what's inside the box changes.
content.title: Key ideas

steps.note: Make a box named `score` and put `100` in it.
Open the `score` box and print what's inside: `100`.
Put `250` in the box. The `100` is thrown away.
Print the box again. This time it holds `250`.

content.title: Watch the box change
content.outro: Same name, two different values, because Python runs the lines in order.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: Line 2 replaces the `5` with `8`. By the time `print` runs, the box only holds `8`.

practice.question: Make a variable named 'age', store your age in it (like 10 or 12), and print it.

quiz.question: What is a variable?
options: A named place to store a value.
A secret code to hack games.
quiz.explain: A variable is a name that stores a value, so the computer can remember it and use it later.

quiz.question: How do you store the number 5 in a variable named 'apples'?
quiz.explain: The name goes on the left and the value goes on the right: `apples = 5`. You can't put the number on the left of the `=`.
